content:
For years, collectors have been keen on memorabilia of Jobs, and a new piece seems set to generate significant interest. This is his eighth-grade science fair project, containing two demonstration circuits, and also a warning note Jobs gave to his teacher.

It has been stored at the Jobs family property in Los Altos ever since, but now it is one of more than 200 lots in the Apple 50th anniversary auction……

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and RR Auctions has held a two-part auction to mark the occasion, named "Steve Jobs & the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction". In the first part, the company's first-ever cheque sold for as much as US$2.4 million.

The second part includes this science fair project.

The warning note may have been to remind that there was a risk of burning out if the circuits ran for too long. At the time of writing, the online bidding price was below US$3,000, but we can expect the situation to change.

There is also a still-working early Apple 1.

As well as a development prototype of the original iPod.
